informal_statement: Issue #234: under any clock calibration (elapsed readings times s > 0, rates times 1/s), age ratios and age-rate products are unchanged, and one scale fits two target ages iff the ratios agree. So the frozen Gupta CCC+TL benchmark's testable content is t(10)/t(0) = 0.2187, t(20)/t(0) = 0.1299 and H0 t0 = 1.98 (total H0). A QLF clock map must reproduce these; matching 26.7 Gyr alone shows nothing. No QLF map is constructed.

approximation_or_regime.name: Clock calibration on the frozen stage-1 result
approximation_or_regime.description: One positive scale on elapsed readings; the frozen ages at z = 0, 10, 20 and H0 from verification/gupta-ccc-tl/result.json.
approximation_or_regime.validity_limits: The z mapping to expansion and tired-light parts is held fixed as part of the model. No QLF clock map, no new data.

strange_loop.name: clock record -> calibrated age -> clock record
strange_loop.conservative_return: Every calibration returns the same ratios and H0 t0; the absolute age is not returned without the scale.
strange_loop.noncircularity_witness: The invariants are fixed before any QLF map exists, so a later map cannot be tuned to them by calibration.
strange_loop.first_order_note: F: QLF_ClockCalibration anchors. N: gupta_scale_free.py on the frozen result.
strange_loop.defeater: A clock calibration law that is not a single multiplicative scale (e.g. epoch-dependent), which would make the ratios calibration-dependent.
